evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the information needed to create a game, not a concrete UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete invitation mechanism (URL) rather than describing the stakeholder need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Explicitly prescribes a specific UI widget for entering the item instead of stating the need to provide/enter the item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a stakeholder need (visibility of items) without prescribing an implementation.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the required capability without mandating a specific UI control or mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (adding items) without prescribing how this must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to edit items; no concrete UI or technical mechanism is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to remove items without prescribing an implementation.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: States desired system behaviour (showing estimates) without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Defines an acceptance rule/behavior, not a technical or UI implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies automated behavior/interaction, but does not prescribe technical mechanisms or concrete UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to record the agreed estimate without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes the capability to re-estimate without prescribing how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a specific import mechanism (spreadsheet) rather than stating the need to bulk-add stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete interaction mechanism (copy/paste from spreadsheet) instead of the stakeholder need to quickly add stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: States a user need (finding previous games) without implying a specific technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Describes a capability to view transcripts; no UI widget or technical implementation is prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete export format (HTML) rather than the need to save a transcript.

evaluations.evidence: as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific file format (CSV) for export instead of stating the general need to export for further processing.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to remove game data; does not mandate a particular deletion mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete account form fields (specific input elements) rather than the higher-level need to create an account.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete authentication mechanism (account name/password) instead of simply stating the need to authenticate.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to update account information without prescribing UI or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove account and associated data; does not specify implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a presentation requirement for the user (local timezone) without prescribing technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific delivery mechanism (email) for reminders instead of the general need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies domain-level option sets (game variants), which are functional choices rather than implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a constraint on number of participants; not a technical mechanism or UI widget specification.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Describes a concrete joining flow relying on a URL and a specific page, prescribing mechanisms rather than the need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's need to view the item; does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States a visibility need without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes a presentation/notification need but does not prescribe how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies expected behavior/interaction timing rather than technical or UI implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Describes allowable user interaction timing; not a technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: States a need for historical visibility without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a requirement for attribution during rounds, not an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a shared-timer capability; this is a functional requirement rather than a low-level UI/technical prescription.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Defines timer behaviour; not a technical or UI implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes a navigation need for prior data without specifying how it should be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistent presentation requirement, not a technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: States allowed interaction timing; no implementation details are prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI element (thumbnail photo) and its placement instead of the underlying need for identification/personalization.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards (XHTML/CSS) to be used, which are implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Requests documentation (definitions) to support shared understanding rather than prescribing technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Asks for a specific implementation action (database indexes) to improve performance rather than stating the performance need.

evaluations.evidence: Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes exact browser versions for compatibility, an implementation/targeting choice rather than a stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Specifies compliance with a particular technical standard (W3C accessibility), which is an implementation-level directive.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a quality-of-service expectation (performance) without mandating technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific technical encoding/format (Unicode) rather than expressing the higher-level need to support multiple languages.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Requests user-facing URL clarity; this is a usability requirement rather than an internal implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need for user-friendly error handling/presentation without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) without prescribing a specific anonymization/storage mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need for usage metrics, not a technical implementation choice.
